title: Zand Dynasty
capsule: The Zand dynasty was an Iranian ruling house founded by Karim Khan Zand, chief of the Lak tribal confederation, who emerged victorious from the chaos following Nader Shah's assassination in 1747. Karim Khan ruled from Shiraz from 1751, deliberately styling himself Vakil al-Ra'ya ('Regent of the People') rather than shah, and presided over a period of relative prosperity and artistic patronage in southern Iran. After his death in 1779, the dynasty was torn by fratricidal succession wars; Lotf Ali Khan, the last Zand ruler, was defeated and killed in 1794 by the Qajar leader Agha Mohammad Khan, who then founded the Qajar dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Zand domain centred on Fars and was loosely defined by tribal allegiance rather than fixed administrative boundaries; its southernmost and northwestern extents fluctuated with the fortunes of competing claimants, making territorial reconstruction approximate.
